proof_skeleton_nl: First prove the pointwise identity on the admissible interval by combining the interval identity K_{n,j}(d)=F_n(J_{n,j}(d)) with substitution through x = J_{n,j}(d). Next specialize the interval identity at d=0, then use the endpoint value J_{n,j}(0)=j/n and rewrite inside F_n. Finally conjoin the two resulting equalities.

steps.derives: For every real d with 0 <= d < 1/n and every real x with x = J_{n,j}(d), one has K_{n,j}(d) = F_n(x).
steps.trivial_justification: Instantiate L2 at the given d to obtain K_{n,j}(d)=F_n(J_{n,j}(d)); then apply L1 with the hypothesis x=J_{n,j}(d) to rewrite F_n(J_{n,j}(d)) as F_n(x). Equality transitivity yields K_{n,j}(d)=F_n(x).

steps.derives: For every positive natural number n and every integer j, one has K_{n,j}(0) = F_n(J_{n,j}(0)).
steps.trivial_justification: Use L3 to verify that d=0 satisfies 0 <= d < 1/n, then instantiate L2 at d=0.

steps.derives: For every positive natural number n and every integer j, one has K_{n,j}(0) = F_n(j/n).
steps.trivial_justification: From L4 obtain J_{n,j}(0)=j/n. Apply L5 with y=j/n to get F_n(J_{n,j}(0))=F_n(j/n). Combine this with A2 by equality transitivity.

steps.derives: For every real d with 0 <= d < 1/n and every real x with x = J_{n,j}(d), one has K_{n,j}(d) = F_n(x), and moreover K_{n,j}(0) = F_n(j/n).
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the conjunction of the two derived claims, so conjunction introduction applies.
